children: Volkswagen job cuts could reach 100,000 by 2030 as the German automaker restructures operations amid Chinese competition, tariffs and weak electric vehicle demand

Volkswagen plans to cut 100,000 jobs worldwide by the end of the decade after management and trade unions agreed to eliminate another 50,000 positions, taking total planned reductions to 100,000, the German automaker said on September 4. The cuts represent around 15 per cent of Volkswagen Group's global workforce and mark the largest restructuring in the automotive industry's history. The group, which includes Audi and Porsche alongside its namesake brand, is seeking to align employment levels with deteriorating market conditions and improve profitability.
Four German Plants Face Uncertain Future

Volkswagen said the long-term future of four major German facilities — Hannover, Emden, Zwickau and Neckarsulm, could not be guaranteed beyond the next decade. Their potential closure would mark the first full-scale shutdown of Volkswagen factories in its home country.

The company has not disclosed the precise timing or geographical distribution of the planned job reductions. Management and unions will need to negotiate implementation, while alternative uses for the affected sites remain under consideration. The restructuring comes amid pressure from US tariffs, sluggish European demand for electric vehicles and intensifying competition from Chinese manufacturers.
Volkswagen Focuses on Cost Reduction, Technology

Chief Executive Oliver Blume said the agreement sent a strong signal about the group's future, as Volkswagen seeks to restore competitiveness through operational reforms and investment. The plan includes a three-digit-billion investment programme over the coming years, with emphasis on research and development, technological upgrades and improved competitiveness.

Volkswagen also intends to reduce the number of businesses and holdings it owns by around one-third, enabling faster decision-making and a more streamlined organisational structure. The automaker is also looking to strengthen its North American presence and expand exports to emerging markets in the Global South as it navigates a challenging global automotive landscape.
